page: Microsoft Azure D2plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processors operating at 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated physical cores matching 2 vCPUs with one thread per core. Memory allocation totals 4.0 GB, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic operations. Local storage includes a 118 GB NVMe solid-state drive, and the VM supports Premium Storage connectivity.

Benchmark evaluation shows competitive single-threaded capabilities alongside expected limits in multi-core throughput due to the dual-core profile. Single-core tests such as stress-ng (2074.19) and Geekbench (1671.0) achieve mid-tier results, while single-threaded gzip compression performs in the top quartile at 33.09 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read memory bandwidth achieves an average 47.98 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the constrained core count, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 4107.17 and Geekbench multi-core scoring 3077.0. Data-plane benchmarks demonstrate static web serving throughput of 4.04 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 4.18 million operations per second.

With 4.0 GB of memory and fast local NVMe storage, the D2plds_v6 offers an entry-level compute tier for lightweight production and dev-test environments. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio prioritizes processing capacity over memory footprint, making it suitable for edge API services, lightweight microservices, caching proxies, and basic CI/CD pipeline workers. The inclusion of bundled fast local scratch storage provides qualitative efficiency for temporary file manipulation, though memory-intensive workloads and heavy parallel execution will require larger instance profiles.

It integrates 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio suited for compute-focused tasks, alongside a bundled 118 GB NVMe solid-state drive for local scratch operations. Benchmark tests indicate solid single-threaded performance, including top-quartile gzip compression at 33.09 GB/sec, moderate Geekbench single-core execution at 1671.0, and 47.98 GB/sec in large-block read memory throughput. Overall multi-core throughput and database metrics reflect its 2-vCPU sizing, recording 4.18 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.04 GB/sec static web throughput. Without discrete GPU acceleration and limited memory capacity, the D2plds_v6 serves efficiently for microservices, lightweight web routing, continuous integration jobs, and basic edge workloads requiring low-latency local storage.
